describes: Sawn Norway pine and spruce, the boards, trims and frames: pale and warm when new, silver-grey within a few years in the weather where no paint keeps the light off.

notes.srgb: New pine and weathered grey wood as screen colours, judged by look against the research's photographs; to check against a measured swatch.
notes.greySpread: Boards reused (an empty house's boarding of old formwork) grey at their own pace: weatherHalfYears times between these, by each board's seed, so a new boarding is grey and brown together and silvered all over in a decade or so. Judged by look: [0.6, 3.0] left every board of a three-year boarding the same grey once the near air was over it (round 3).
notes.nailStain: Steel nails rust and the rust runs down the grain below them, a little further each year up to downM (6 years), two nails fromTopM below a board's top (into the head casing under its cap: a board runs past the cap by its end over) and acrossM either side of its middle; the streak widthMm wide at the nail, spreading to the second at its end. Common knowledge, assumed; judged by look (6 mm was under a pixel at eye level, round 3).
notes.boardingValueSpread: Reused boards come from mixed stock (heart and sap, planed and rough, a film of cement on some): each a share lighter or darker than the next, by its seed. Judged by look: without it the near air over a dark boarding left one flat grey (round 3).
notes.weatherHalfYears: Bare wood greys in sunlight within one to three years: half the way in this many years at full weather.
notes.water: Its water profile as the town's (Shaders/Water.hlsl, Overstory.World.WaterPack): how much it darkens wet, how glossy its wet film, how long it holds water, how readily run-off stains it. Bare weathered wood drinks rain and goes dark, stays wet, stains. Judged by look.
